Both query modes validate all ZIP metadata and selected root DEX payloads only; unselected payload integrity is unverified. `X64StringInstructions.def` also owns ordinary-RAM `CMPS/SCAS` at 8/16/32/64 bits with `REPE/REPNE`. Every element validates both complete read operands before observers, updates all six arithmetic flags, and stops on the first matching termination condition. A data fault restores the flags from entry to this uninterrupted REP while retaining completed pointer/count changes; a public resume starts from the published CPU state. Stops and observer exceptions leave the current element untouched. Early termination never reads the next element. FS/GS affects only the CMPS source; SCAS leaves the accumulator and unused source register unchanged. Device operands and ambiguous inactive 32-bit upper halves remain excluded. `X64StringComparisonTests.cpp` compares independent host instructions, flags, direction, aliases, wrapping, permissions and recovery; its Linux x64 signal oracle checks actual fault-time registers. The original WDK resource driver executes both conditional-repeat forms at all four widths through `driver_resource_strings.def`. See the [Intel instruction reference](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html).

`X64StringInstructions.def` owns ordinary-RAM `MOVS/STOS/LODS` at 8/16/32/64 bits; `CLD/STD` controls direction without changing other flags. Each REP element validates the entire operand before observations and commits at one restart boundary. Earlier completed elements survive a later fault; cancellation or observer failure leaves the current element untouched. FS/GS applies only to the source, after address-size truncation. AL/AX loads preserve upper bits and EAX loads zero-extend. Zero-count address-size-32 REP requires zero upper count bits and, for MOVS/STOS, zero upper participating address bits: real CPU implementations differ otherwise. REPNE on MOVS/STOS/LODS and STOS/LODS device operands remain unsupported. `X64StringTransferTests.cpp` uses independent host instructions for widths, direction, overlap and zero counts, with separate checks for permissions, aliases, wraparound, faults and resumption. The original WDK resource driver executes all four STOS/LODS widths through `driver_resource_strings.def`.

`WhpResourceCache.h` separates logical CPU state from WHP partitions. The runtime keeps one active native partition: consecutive steps on the same CPU reuse it; switching CPU retires the old partition before rebuilding mappings, a virtual processor and full state. Lease acquisition observes cancellation and the current deadline; retiring an inactive CPU cannot destroy another CPU's partition. x64 preserves the host's default XSAVE feature set and validates the effective partition via `WHvGetPartitionProperty`; it does not clear dependent features to force a reduced mask. Cooperative CPU switching does not provide parallel hardware SMP.

API providers have no fabricated DLL handles. Filesystem search, non-ASCII paths, `LoadLibraryEx` flags, cyclic imports and reentrant transitions of an already initializing or unloading module remain unsupported.

Native Windows x64 CI with Unicorn disabled passes all 359 required checks: 131 CPU checks, 224 driver outcomes from 26 built-in images, 46 WDK images and 40 scenario cases at both preferred and relocated bases, plus four SEH boundary checks. Verified at 9d4c130c2f11d95a2f80f1055dfdbb34de07715c (GitHub Actions 36981864458), with complete inventory/JUnit reconciliation; this does not establish arbitrary-driver or native ARM64 compatibility. Detailed per-feature and public-API tests marked Linux-only retain that narrower evidence scope.

`DriverImage.def` declares strict PE size/alignment limits and diagnostic text; pointer widths come from `DriverProfile.def`. `DriverImage.cpp` owns validation and relocation, with unchanged accepted images and error messages.

Independent MDL pages support MmAllocatePagesForMdl/Ex, MmFreePagesFromMdl and MmProtectMdlSystemAddress over the bounded physical arena. Range/chunk constraints, cache identity, partial ownership, user/system aliases and release dependencies share existing physical-page authority. KernelMode pool locks make precisely pinned paged memory resident; backend page permissions remain authoritative for all mapping views.

Message interrupt assignments preserve explicit per-message addresses/data/vectors/levels/affinity/polarity. PDO-wide message registration exposes real read-only interrupt tables and independent or unified synchronization. Passive ISR waits retain ownership, serialize repeated arrivals and allow independent frames and DPCs to progress; occurrence and delivery timestamps remain distinct.

KMDF 1.33 implements 117 table APIs, including WdfInterruptCreate, WdfInterruptQueueDpcForIsr, WdfInterruptQueueWorkItemForIsr, WdfInterruptSynchronize, WdfInterruptAcquireLock, WdfInterruptReleaseLock, WdfInterruptEnable, WdfInterruptDisable, WdfInterruptWdmGetInterrupt, WdfInterruptGetInfo and WdfInterruptGetDevice. Framework interrupt objects use assigned line/MSI resources and existing WDM connection, epoch, lock and IRQL authority. ISR/synchronization run at assigned DIRQL or PASSIVE_LEVEL; passive GetInfo reports PASSIVE_LEVEL. Excess objects remain unassigned. Explicit enable/disable invokes genuine driver callbacks without inventing hardware pulses.

WDF interrupt DPCs/work items share scheduler FIFOs and retain ownership until return. Normal interrupts enable after D0Entry and disable/drain before D0Exit. ReportInactiveOnPowerDown and WdfInterruptReportInactive/WdfInterruptReportActive retain the original connection with explicit active-state eligibility; final hardware release disconnects. Passive CanWakeDevice requires an assigned wake_capable resource and armed policy, remains enabled in Dx and retains explicit pulse delivery until physical D0 and successful D0Entry. Wake interrupts are not reported inactive; no hardware pulse or wake capability is inferred.

WdfSpinLockCreate/WdfSpinLockAcquire/WdfSpinLockRelease share executive spin-lock ownership and IRQL restoration; WdfWaitLockCreate/WdfWaitLockAcquire/WdfWaitLockRelease use nonrecursive dispatcher locks owned by actual threads, normal kernel APC-disable state, waiter retention and infinite/relative/absolute/zero deadlines. Zero-timeout acquisition requires IRQL below DISPATCH_LEVEL; other acquisition requires PASSIVE_LEVEL. External WDFSPINLOCK/WDFWAITLOCK objects are retained by interrupt objects and deletion validates held locks, waiters and parent lifetimes. Interrupt-assigned spin locks require interrupt lock APIs. WdfObjectAcquireLock/WdfObjectReleaseLock use the device/queue callback lock. Automatic I/O/file/cancel/interrupt-deferred serialization retains the selected synchronization owner through wait and callback return; same-thread automatic callbacks may recurse, explicit object-lock acquisition may not. Passive callback locks can wait; dispatch callback locks raise IRQL and reject blocking contention. DPC/work-item automatic serialization requires a compatible parent execution level. Existing API-specific IRQL bounds remain in force; legacy WdfRequestMarkCancelable supports IRQL through DISPATCH_LEVEL with real callback-level scheduling.

Optional pnp_devices parent_id declares the provider devnode graph using configured IDs; array order is irrelevant and omission creates an independent root. Native and JSON preflight reject invalid IDs, unknown parents, self-links and cycles before PDO allocation. Observed parent_id and parent_pdo retain identity after provider retirement. Child START requires a present, Started parent in physical D0 with no pending lifecycle or power transition. Parent STOP and SurpriseRemoval require children to leave active PnP states and drain pending transitions and WAIT_WAKE; parent REMOVE requires every child provider to retire first. No implicit cascade occurs. The graph does not create WDM attachment or WDF object-parent edges and does not expose guest bus-enumeration APIs.

Declared parent_id relationships support KMDF Sx child wake. ArmForWakeIfChildrenAreArmedForWake and IndicateChildWakeOnParentWake are independent Boolean settings. EvtDeviceArmWakeFromSxWithReason receives separate own-device and child reasons, including (FALSE, TRUE) when only children require wake. Only successfully armed Sx children with a real retained WAIT_WAKE contribute; the parent captures their PDO and START epoch. Parent wake completes those retained IRPs after validating the whole batch and propagates recursively only through devices that opt in. Disabled, disarmed, failed and restarted children do not receive an invented wake. Successful WAIT_WAKE reports record the original source in nullable wake_source_device_id and wake_source_pdo; each device still needs explicit Working and D0 requests through its own response FIFO. Arm children before their parent enters Sx/Dx. New child arming is rejected before creating WAIT_WAKE when its direct parent is already in Sx/Dx with either child-aware setting enabled. Canceling the last captured child also cancels a child-only parent's retained WAIT_WAKE and executes its disarm callback once; a parent with its own wake reason or a completed wake keeps normal D0 disarm ordering. This profile uses declared provider topology; guest bus PDO enumeration and raw WDM child-wake callbacks remain unsupported.

Power-policy APIs: WdfDeviceInitSetPowerPolicyEventCallbacks, WdfDeviceAssignS0IdleSettings, WdfDeviceAssignSxWakeSettings, WdfDeviceStopIdleNoTrack, WdfDeviceResumeIdleNoTrack, WdfDeviceStopIdleActual, WdfDeviceResumeIdleActual. Driver-managed idle policy supports an explicit positive timeout in milliseconds, IdleCannotWake/IdleCanWake and no user override. S0 and Sleeping3 wake execute the registered arm, triggered and disarm callbacks around a real retained WAIT_WAKE IRP. StopIdle/ResumeIdle hold balanced, nestable power references; StopIdle(TRUE) requires PASSIVE_LEVEL and suspends the actual calling frame until D0 completion, while FALSE and ResumeIdle permit IRQL through DISPATCH_LEVEL. Synchronous StopIdle from a managed-queue callback or during power-down fails as a deadlock. The S0 idle and Sx wake assignment APIs permit IRQL through DISPATCH_LEVEL; callback registration requires PASSIVE_LEVEL. Sx wake records a signal and still requires an explicit system Working request. PowerUpIdleDeviceOnSystemWake governs whether a non-wake-capable idle device remains in Dx until activity. SystemManagedIdleTimeout and SystemManagedIdleTimeoutWithHint default to one framework-owned F0 component; idle alone does not synthesize OS power-down permission. STOP/REMOVE unregister, and restart creates a fresh owner. General PEP/platform policy and automatic failed-device reenumeration remain unsupported. Scenarios explicitly declare PDO wake_capabilities: {s0, sx} as Booleans. READ/WRITE/IOCTL requests may provide power_policy_events: [{device_id, after_100ns, action}], with framework actions idle, active or wake and the explicit PoFx decisions described above. Idle starts the driver’s timeout; active requests D0 when needed, and wake requires an armed source. Reports retain source_request_index, event_index, device_id, captured device_epoch, action, due_at_100ns and occurred_at_100ns; events cannot bind to a later restart. D0/D2/D3 requests consume requested_device_power responses and report origin: "framework_power_policy". The independent origin: "framework_wait_wake" IRP remains pending until wake or disarm and does not consume that FIFO. A completed cancellation of this WAIT_WAKE is a valid expected outcome.

Only an absolute, read-only 8-byte access to `GS:[0x188]` exposes the current logical thread’s borrowed opaque identity. Compiler forms such as `MOV` and `CMP` execute as the original backend instruction, with their original register and flag effects. Nested callbacks on that thread see the same object; unrelated threads remain distinct, and modeled system threads use their existing object. The private processor view supplies this field without modeling a complete KPCR or granting thread-structure access or reference ownership. Other GS offsets, all FS accesses, indexed or partial-width reads and stores remain unsupported.

WdfDeviceWdmAssignPowerFrameworkSettings at KMDF 1.33 slot 425 supports copied custom single-component Fx settings once before the first START completes, after successful system-managed idle assignment at PASSIVE_LEVEL. Guest component callbacks execute through existing continuations; omitted callbacks use framework defaults. PoFxDeviceFlags must be zero, DirectedPoFxEnabled must be WdfFalse, and PEP power-control callbacks remain unsupported. EvtDeviceWdmPostPoFxRegisterDevice runs before management starts; failure fails START and suspends running self-managed I/O before hardware release. The handle remains valid until EvtDeviceWdmPrePoFxUnregisterDevice returns; STOP/REMOVE quiesces unissued decisions and drains existing component callbacks before D0Exit; restart obtains a new handle. Pending PoFx device-power acknowledgements reject teardown before hardware changes until the real D-state transaction completes; this serialization boundary belongs to the profile, not the general WDK contract. Public framework-handle operations are limited to PoFxCompleteIdleCondition, PoFxCompleteIdleState and component latency/residency/wake hints. Framework-owned activity, device-power acknowledgements and registration lifetime cannot be changed by raw guest PoFx calls in this profile; this is a model boundary rather than a WDK prohibition. Power-managed requests remain held until active F0 and completed D0 recovery.

WDM PoFx v1 registration copies component and idle-state descriptions and retains the PDO. Balanced activation references, callback entry, acknowledgement and return have separate ownership; blocking calls continue on the actual calling thread. Latency, residency, wake and idle-timeout hints constrain explicit component_idle_state and power_not_required decisions; they never synthesize Windows policy. Events bind the current registration and captured START epoch. PoFx v2/v3, directed power management, and arbitrary platform power-control requests remain unsupported.

Optional PDO d3cold requires Boolean supported, enabled_by_default, wake_s0 and wake_sx facts for a dedicated supply; cold wake also requires the matching wake_capabilities. ExcludeD3Cold True retains D3hot, False permits declared support, Default follows the provider default. Missing cold wake leaves an armed device in D3hot. Only successful D3hot-to-cold entry advances power generation and resets configured MMIO values before D0 access. Assignment epochs and mappings survive; MMIO/DMA still require physical D0. Outstanding DMA transactions, mappings and channels block cold entry, while idle adapters/common RAM buffers may remain. Shared rails and firmware behavior are not inferred.

The optional scenario-root service_name overrides the base configuration; omission preserves the caller’s service name. It must contain 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, _ or -, and applies equally to CLI, C and Python scenario JSON.

WDF request/object APIs explicitly supported through DISPATCH_LEVEL are WdfObjectDereferenceActual, WdfRequestComplete, WdfRequestCompleteWithInformation, WdfRequestRetrieveInputBuffer, WdfRequestRetrieveOutputBuffer, WdfRequestRetrieveInputMemory, WdfRequestRetrieveOutputMemory, WdfRequestRetrieveInputWdmMdl, WdfRequestRetrieveOutputWdmMdl, WdfRequestGetInformation, WdfRequestSetInformation, WdfRequestGetIoQueue, WdfRequestGetFileObject, WdfRequestWdmGetIrp, WdfRequestGetParameters, WdfRequestGetStatus, WdfRequestMarkCancelable, WdfRequestMarkCancelableEx, WdfRequestUnmarkCancelable, WdfRequestIsCanceled, WdfMemoryGetBuffer. WdfObjectGetTypedContextWorker, WdfObjectContextGetObject and WdfObjectReferenceActual also support modeled interrupt IRQLs without invoking passive callbacks. Request completion and final object dereference above PASSIVE_LEVEL schedule actual cleanup, destruction and subsequent framework delivery in a separate FrameworkPassive continuation at PASSIVE_LEVEL. Its WDM device ownership persists through queueing, suspension, nested callbacks and final scheduler retirement. Legacy WdfRequestMarkCancelable selects inline or deferred callbacks using the queue execution level and current callback lock ownership; all other APIs retain their existing IRQL restrictions. The genuine WDK driver_kmdf_pnp.c interrupt extension covers normal/CFG and preferred/rebased line, MSI, passive, PrepareHardware creation, enable failure and reconnection; optional artifacts reuse NEVERD_KMDF_PNP_FIXTURE and NEVERD_KMDF_PNP_CFG_FIXTURE. Linux-only execution does not establish general WDF compatibility.

KernelFrameworkPower sequences self-managed Init/Suspend/Restart/Flush/Cleanup and pre/post interrupt D0 callbacks. Ordinary device D3/D0 retains resources. Default FDO power policy consumes explicit requested_device_power templates for Sleeping3/Working Query/Set device children, reporting framework_power_policy origins and response indices. Driver-managed D3hot idle and S0/Sleeping3 wake use real retained WAIT_WAKE IRPs and the same power-request authority; automatic failed-device reenumeration is not modeled.

requires NEVERD_ENABLE_DRIVER_EMULATION=ON; this opt-in profile executes x64 WDM initialization and explicitly requested create, buffered/direct IOCTL, read/write, cleanup, close, configured AddDevice/resource-free or register-bank PnP, explicit pageable Query/Set power and unload phases through Unicorn, without host kernel loading or host OS API forwarding

only the documented native PE32+ loading profile and finite kernel API subset are modeled; unknown imports are lazy traps and stop at first execution or exported-data read, while unmodeled CPU environment operations, opaque object state, malformed images and unsupported loader requirements fail explicitly

WDM stacks contain guest-owned DEVICE_OBJECTs and optionally a separately owned scenario PDO. IoAttachDeviceToDeviceStack returns the previous top and derives StackSize/AlignmentRequirement without changing the NextDevice inventory or buffer flags. IoDetachDevice receives the saved lower at PASSIVE_LEVEL; attach permits DISPATCH_LEVEL. Named lower FILE_OBJECT/report identity stays distinct from top dispatch and top READ/WRITE flags; retained routes survive detach/delete through dispatch return. Internal holds do not inflate the open-handle ReferenceCount.

IofCallDriver and the IoCallDriver helper dispatch to the exact retained target; genuine inline Copy/Skip/SetCompletion operate on the original bounded guest IRP stack. Completion clears consumed lower slots before upper callbacks and separates lower NTSTATUS, callback control results and final IoStatus. Success/error/cancel masks and pending propagation are modeled, including propagation after STATUS_PENDING dispatch returns; invoked callbacks own propagation. STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED and nested completion preserve packet/MDL/buffer lifetime until terminal unwind, with exactly-once retirement.

IoAllocateIrp and IoFreeIrp support caller-owned packets through DISPATCH_LEVEL with ChargeQuota=FALSE. First IoCallDriver validates the packet and captures the exact lower device route. This bounded path supports kernel IRP_MJ_INTERNAL_DEVICE_CONTROL with METHOD_NEITHER buffers owned by the driver; it does not create a user file or copy user buffers. The guest executes real completion and cancel routines. Freeing the packet inside its completion requires STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED; packet access ends immediately, while dispatch and callback metadata remain until their frames return. An unsent packet can be freed directly; leaked, double-freed, foreign or still-owned packets fail explicitly. Arbitrary packet reuse, other caller-created request formats, IoBuildDeviceIoControlRequest remain unsupported. Observed caller requests use kind: "internal_ioctl", origin: "driver_allocated_irp" and file: null, preserving code, irp, dispatch/I/O status, cancellation time and exact information_hex. Native and JSON scenarios reject internal_ioctl before image loading; only actual guest allocation and dispatch create these rows. Except for the explicit USB idle protocol, the lower target must be a live guest WDM device; submit with a completion routine enabled for success, error and cancellation. The genuine driver_wdm_owned_irp.c fixture uses NEVERD_WDM_OWNED_IRP_FIXTURE / NEVERD_WDM_OWNED_IRP_CFG_FIXTURE. The [caller-owned IRP scenario](examples/driver-owned-irp-scenario.json) exercises delayed completion. Normal/active-CFG images run at preferred/rebased addresses; C API/CLI checks preserve independent kernel-origin rows. Missing artifacts skip explicitly; execution evidence remains Linux-only.

KernelGuestCall uses subsystem-owner tags and local tokens for nested WDM/WDF continuations, preserving parent CPU frames and inherited IRQL. WDF target forwarding outside direct FDO/PDO file lifecycle, attachment to live stacks, intermediate detach, changed forwarded major functions, targets outside retained routes, additional PnP operations and other hardware/resource models remain unsupported.

Optional genuine-WDK driver_wdm_stack.c images use NEVERD_WDM_STACK_FIXTURE and NEVERD_WDM_STACK_CFG_FIXTURE. Model/native/public tests cover Copy and Skip, buffered READ/WRITE and file lifecycle, IOCTL completion ordering, worker/DPC completion, MPR waits with direct MDLs, nested completion, malformed cursors and normal/active-CFG rebasing. Missing artifacts skip explicitly; evidence remains Linux-only.

Public DriverPnp.h and DeviceLifecycle.def own lifecycle enums; pnp_devices explicitly supplies up to 64 unique case-sensitive ASCII IDs of 1-64 bytes (leading alphanumeric, then alphanumeric/_/-/.), resource_free or register_bank bus, D0 device power and working system power. No missing hardware/power facts are guessed. Ordinary device_id and device selectors are exclusive; PnP requires device_id, minor and bus_completion and rejects file/transfer/cancellation fields even when zero. JSON/native preflight share the same contract.

The eight public common PnP minors are Start, QueryRemove, CancelRemove, Remove, QueryStop, Stop, CancelStop and SurpriseRemoval. Every configured bus completion requires an explicit final 32-bit status, rejects STATUS_PENDING, and accepts optional nonnegative delay_100ns through INT64_MAX from actual provider receipt. Stop/CancelStop/SurpriseRemoval/CancelRemove/Remove require exactly STATUS_SUCCESS (0). Shared devicePnpFinalStatusError validates both configured bus policy and final guest completion. QueryStop STATUS_RESOURCE_REQUIREMENTS_CHANGED (0x119) is explicitly unsupported because it requests resource requery. Other PnP operations, general power policy, resource rebalance, relations/capabilities, general hardware and broader KMDF PnP remain unsupported.

After successful DriverEntry, each configured PDO invokes the actual guest AddDevice callback once in add_device:<ID>. Provider-owned PDO/DRIVER_OBJECT inventory remains separate from the guest driver and cannot be deleted, mutated or impersonated by guest code. Successful filters may decline attachment. Failed AddDevice records its status and retires only a clean provider; new guest devices left behind, including detached leaks, cause ModelError without fabricated cleanup.

Forwarded WDM CREATE/CLEANUP/CLOSE accept an explicit delayed bus_completion and execute the real guest completion routine after the lower deadline, preserving pending propagation and final-status ownership. PnP IRPs share the existing captured route, guest stack and completion authority; they are KernelMode, file-free and initially STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED. Only actual provider receipt consumes the configured response; timed completion participates in the virtual scheduler without inventing a guest callback. Final upper completion owns lifecycle commit/rollback and may differ from the recorded bus status; successful PnP requires actual completed bus forwarding. Early Start/QueryStop/QueryRemove guest failure can leave bus observations null.

Ordinary CREATE/READ/WRITE/IOCTL/CLEANUP/CLOSE reach real guest dispatch outside Removing/Removed; model stop, remove-pending and power state do not synthesize an I/O refusal. Guest code may complete software operations, reject them or hold them. Immutable FDO/PDO and FILE_OBJECT lifecycle identity survives detach. Pending WDM transfers can overlap only through explicit batching across files or on one asynchronous file; a held IRP without a currently available producer still cannot wait for a later scenario start or cleanup request and is an explicit stalled ModelError. Normal Remove from Started still requires successful query; closed files and drained earlier requests before Remove are bounded-profile restrictions. Providers must be absent before unload; guest and provider retirement remain independent.

Reports preserve configuration.pnp_devices and observed pnp_devices id/pdo/add_device_status/attached/pnp_state/provider_present. Attached is current and false after removal. AddDevice failures affect scenario_success without replacing DriverEntry nt_status. Requests add nullable device_id/pnp; PnP file is null, with minor/state_before/state_after and nullable bus_status/bus_received_at_100ns/bus_completed_at_100ns. Configured status appears only at actual bus completion; receipt time is independent and legacy field types are preserved.

Original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_pnp.c uses optional NEVERD_WDM_PNP_FIXTURE/NEVERD_WDM_PNP_CFG_FIXTURE; native normal/active-CFG rebasing covers AddDevice, file I/O, orderly/delayed removal, start/query failure and clean/leaking AddDevice failure. C API/CLI test seven-request delayed PnP reports. Missing artifacts skip explicitly; evidence remains Linux-only and does not establish general PnP/power support. Additional native cases exercise query-stop/cancel-stop/stop/restart, surprise removal, software I/O in pause/remove-pending states, guest failure after surprise, independent PDO/file identities, mixed AddDevice outcomes and an independent control device. C API/CLI normal/CFG execution also covers a 16-request stop/restart/surprise sequence and preflight rejection of resource requery.

KMDF caller-context preprocessing for buffered/direct/neither READ, WRITE and IOCTL runs at PASSIVE_LEVEL in the requestor process; the callback must complete or explicitly enqueue once before the configured default queue delivers I/O. For METHOD_NEITHER and neither READ/WRITE, unsafe accessors expose original scenario user buffers only there; WDF probe-and-lock checks page rights, pins request-owned physical bytes, and WdfMemoryGetBuffer returns a system alias usable by the queue outside requestor context. Completion releases aliases and pins; declared user_buffers support embedded pointers within the current request, while arbitrary user mappings remain unsupported.

KMDF 1.33 exact-version binding preserves real FxDriverEntry execution, separate WDFLDR module identity and 458 distinct function-table entries; only 117 documented table APIs plus WdfVersionBind/WdfVersionUnbind are modeled, and other reached entries remain unsupported_api traps; downlevel negotiation, class extensions and WdfLdrQueryInterface are unsupported

KMDF non-PnP drivers, generic objects, control devices, manual, sequential and finite or unlimited parallel default and nondefault queues, and incoming requests share typed contexts and guest cleanup/destroy callbacks at PASSIVE_LEVEL; nested continuations preserve caller CPU state and stack. Failed DriverEntry unregister cleans objects without EvtDriverUnload; adding references after cleanup is unsupported. Direct KMDF FDO/PDO pairs support resource-free and configured register-bank devices; device/queue automatic parent synchronization uses inherited passive/dispatch callback locks; Managed PnP queues invoke EvtIoStop for driver-owned requests before D0 exit; WdfRequestStopAcknowledge requeues for delivery after restart or retains ownership for EvtIoResume after D0 entry. Framework-queued requests stay parked through STOP. Returning without completion or acknowledgment waits for the request to finish; a transition with no available completion producer stalls explicitly.

KMDF PnP drivers execute EvtDriverDeviceAdd once per configured PDO with a framework-owned initializer. WdfDeviceCreate builds the direct FDO/PDO pair; WdfDeviceInitSetDeviceType passes an optional 32-bit device type to the authoritative WDM DEVICE_OBJECT creator, defaulting to FILE_DEVICE_UNKNOWN; WdfDeviceInitSetExclusive passes the initial DO_EXCLUSIVE flag to that same device creator, but an exclusive PnP FDO does not make the named PDO or whole stack exclusive; IoCreateDevice also stores caller-supplied system or vendor device types as metadata, without modeling type-specific I/O priority boosts; WdfFdoInitWdmGetPhysicalDevice, WdfDeviceWdmGetPhysicalDevice, WdfDeviceWdmGetAttachedDevice, WdfWdmDeviceGetWdfDeviceHandle and WdfDeviceGetDriver preserve provider, stack and binding identity. A failed AddDevice automatically deletes created WDF devices and runs cleanup/destroy callbacks before provider retirement. Completed Remove runs WDF deletion before captured-route and PDO retirement. PnP queues accept WdfUseDefault/WdfTrue power management or WdfFalse driver-managed dispatch. WdfDeviceInitSetPnpPowerEventCallbacks accepts PrepareHardware, D0Entry, D0Exit, ReleaseHardware, QueryStop, QueryRemove and SurpriseRemoval in the exact 144-byte KMDF 1.33 structure. Resource-free WDFCMRESLIST handles support GetCount=0 and GetDescriptor=NULL; configured register-bank lists expose read-only raw/translated CM_PARTIAL_RESOURCE_DESCRIPTOR entries through ReleaseHardware, then retire their guest storage. After provider START, PrepareHardware precedes D0Entry before IRP completion; failed PrepareHardware or D0Entry becomes the START status and still runs ReleaseHardware. STOP, surprise removal or removal from D0 runs D0Exit then ReleaseHardware before completion. Power-managed queues report WdfIoQueuePnpHeld outside D0. Before D0Exit, power-managed queues wait for driver-owned requests to complete: EvtIoStop may complete, acknowledge or return while an existing worker finishes the request, and a queue without EvtIoStop also waits. True acknowledgment requeues for delivery after restart, while false retains ownership for EvtIoResume after D0Entry. A request with no completion producer stalls explicitly. Framework-queued requests resume delivery after START, including without hardware callbacks. QueryStop/QueryRemove run before the bus and may wait or reject the query without a bus observation or power transition; STATUS_PENDING and STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED are invalid callback results. SurpriseRemoval is a void notification before lower forwarding. Unmodeled resource types, resource mutation, other PnP events remain unsupported. A genuine WDK driver maps translated memory with MmMapIoSpace in PrepareHardware, unmaps it in ReleaseHardware, and final PnP completion rejects leaked mappings. The original WDK-linked driver_kmdf_pnp.c fixture covers normal/active-CFG rebasing, successful and failed AddDevice, start/file I/O/remove/unload and optional EvtDriverUnload via native and C API/CLI tests; evidence remains Linux-only.

Control devices require a copied printable-ASCII name and exact universal-access SDDL D:P(A;;GA;;;WD); other DACLs need an unmodeled caller token. WdfDeviceInitSetExclusive makes a named control device exclusive until its first open file closes; the open check uses the named object rather than the upper dispatch target. Initializers are consumed only on success, partial creation is rolled back, and device/link ownership uses the WDM namespace; FinishInitializing gates delivery. Pending I/O or other live references prevent unsupported deletion/draining.

The 96-byte WDF_IO_QUEUE_CONFIG supports manual, sequential and finite or unlimited parallel default and nondefault queues with inherited, device, queue or none synchronization scope and passive/dispatch execution levels; control-device queues are not power-managed, while PnP queues honor their tri-state power policy. Parallel dispatch uses NumberOfPresentedRequests=-1 for unlimited delivery or a positive finite limit. Requests beyond a finite or sequential presentation limit wait in FIFO order until a presented request completes, leaves the queue or is canceled. A manual default queue retains incoming requests without callback delivery. WdfIoQueueStop pauses delivery while still accepting requests; WdfIoQueueStart resumes waiting automatic callbacks, and WdfIoQueueGetState reports queued/delivered counts and readiness bits. Retrieval while stopped returns STATUS_WDF_PAUSED; a stop-completion callback receives its context after all previously delivered requests complete or leave the queue, while queued waiters do not block it; duplicate pending callback registration fails explicitly. WdfIoQueueDrain rejects new arrivals with STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_STATE while delivering already queued requests; its callback waits for both queued and driver-owned counts to reach zero, forwarding into a drained queue returns STATUS_WDF_BUSY, and WdfIoQueueStart restores acceptance. WdfIoQueuePurge also rejects arrivals, completes queued requests with STATUS_CANCELLED after cleanup, requests cancellation of marked driver-owned IRPs through their callbacks, and notifies only after queued, driver-owned and active cancel callback work has finished. WdfIoQueueStopSynchronously, WdfIoQueueDrainSynchronously and WdfIoQueuePurgeSynchronously suspend the caller until their respective delivered or queued-and-delivered work retires; purge waits through marked-request cancellation callbacks. A synchronous wait with no completion producer fails explicitly as stalled. WdfIoQueueStopAndPurge and WdfIoQueueStopAndPurgeSynchronously cancel requests queued at call time and marked driver-owned requests while keeping acceptance enabled and delivery paused. Later arrivals remain queued and do not delay the state callback or synchronous wait. Stop and StopSynchronously restore acceptance after a prior drain or purge. WdfRequestForwardToIoQueue transfers driver ownership to another same-device queue; an automatic destination presents its own matching callback when capacity permits, or completes with STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST after a slot opens if no handler matches. WdfIoQueueRetrieveNextRequest restores ownership from manual or sequential queues in FIFO order and returns STATUS_NO_MORE_ENTRIES with NULL when empty; parallel retrieval returns STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_STATE. WdfRequestRequeue puts an unmarked retrieved request at the head of its manual queue. Cancellation of a still-queued request removes it and completes with STATUS_CANCELLED, executing cleanup callbacks before IRP retirement. Accepted requests mark the same IRP pending and return STATUS_PENDING independently of void callback RAX. Default file handling completes CREATE/CLEANUP/CLOSE with Information=0; zero READ/WRITE and missing default-queue handlers follow explicit framework policy.

WdfIoQueueReadyNotify registers one EvtIoQueueState callback for a manual queue; it receives WDFQUEUE and WDFCONTEXT at PASSIVE_LEVEL when the queued count changes from empty to nonempty, including while earlier retrieved requests remain driver-owned. Registration on a nonempty queue may notify immediately, while a stopped queue defers until Start. Duplicate registration or deregistration before Stop returns STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST; NULL deregisters after Stop.

WdfIoQueueFindRequest searches a manual queue without taking ownership and adds a framework reference on success; WdfObjectDereferenceActual releases that reference. WdfIoQueueRetrieveFoundRequest transfers ownership only while the request remains queued; cancellation removal returns STATUS_NOT_FOUND. Optional WDF_REQUEST_PARAMETERS reuse WdfRequestGetParameters layout. Live framework file-object filters are supported for manual queue searches; retrieval by file object takes a matching request from a manual or sequential queue and preserves the output on a miss.

EvtIoCanceledOnQueue receives WDFQUEUE and WDFREQUEST for a request previously delivered to the driver and then forwarded or requeued, or explicitly enqueued from caller context. A never-delivered queued request is framework-completed with STATUS_CANCELLED without that callback. Cancellation transfers an eligible request to driver ownership; it must be completed inside the callback or later and cannot be requeued. Purge and queue-state notification wait for the callback and driver-owned request to finish.

The 40-byte WDF_REQUEST_PARAMETERS and input/output accessors preserve logical lengths, buffered aliases and existing direct MDL mappings; direct IOCTL input remains buffered. Completion validates first, then runs cleanup and child destruction before IRP retirement; new buffer/parameter accessors stop once completion begins, while saved buffers remain valid through cleanup. External WDF references preserve context without retaining completed IRP/queue ownership.

KMDF control-device READ/WRITE/IOCTL cancellation uses optional cancel_after_100ns, a nonnegative JSON integer at most INT64_MAX relative to submission in virtual 100 ns units. Zero acts after routing and before the guest I/O callback, including after caller-context enqueue and queue routing, unless routing completed first; completion before cancellation leaves cancel_requested_at_100ns null, otherwise reports record the actual absolute virtual time. KeInitializeSpinLock and five executive acquire/release/try APIs model resident, aligned x64 locks on CPU0. Physical intervals cannot overflow; translated intervals never overlap globally, raw intervals cannot overlap within one PDO, and register intervals must fit without overlap. Widths1/2/4 and offsets/translated addresses are naturally aligned; values fit their declared width. Empty register arrays explicitly leave no accessible offsets.

Register-bank START receives separate read-only packed raw and translated CM_RESOURCE_LISTs with corresponding ordered Memory descriptors, one full header, Internal/bus0/version1/revision1, DeviceExclusive and READ_WRITE range flags. ResourceFree retains null lists. Each START from NotStarted/Stopped creates a new fixed-assignment epoch, published only at actual successful provider START completion before upper callbacks. Bank values initialize from the PDO configuration and persist across unmap, STOP, restart and D3hot. Failed START or successful STOP/REMOVE requires driver unmap before terminal IRP completion, allowing upper completion callbacks to unmap first; no implicit mapping cleanup hides a leak. Surprise arrival disables hardware/new maps immediately while allowing unmap.

KernelResources is the sole physical-assignment, epoch, presence and power authority. KernelMMIO owns bank values and aliases; KernelInterrupts owns connections, locks, pulses and level-source assertions. Actual successful provider device-SET completion updates hardware accessibility before final upper lifecycle completion: D2/D3 forbid register transactions but permits mapping, D0 additionally requires a live assignment. This register-bank provider preserves register values and mappings through D2 and D3hot. Explicit successful D3cold advances a separate power generation and restores configured register values on authorized D0 access without changing the assignment epoch or aliases. PoSetPowerState notification remains a separate fact.

MmMapIoSpace uses NonCached; MmMapIoSpaceEx uses PAGE_NOCACHE with PAGE_READONLY/PAGE_READWRITE. Both accept exact translated subranges within one assignment and preserve page offset. Aliases share register state with independent permissions; MmUnmapIoSpace requires the original base/length. Monotonic address reservations prevent stale mapping reuse. Mapping/window or configured memory-budget exhaustion returns NULL; backend failures remain explicit errors. No arbitrary physical RAM, execute/cache variants, PCI configuration, ports, other interrupt modes, resource rebalance or other DMA interfaces is implied.

GuestMemory and UnicornBackend preflight whole original accesses and share a first-fault/stop latch with MMIO callbacks, preventing Unicorn width splitting or post-stop callbacks from producing effects. Declared device-register scalar1/2/4 and real REP element transactions execute; holes, wrong widths, unaligned/partial/cross-mapping accesses, RO writes and instruction fetches fail before register effects. Modeled API memory accesses must also fit one aligned 1/2/4-byte transaction; larger bulk spans fail instead of being split into register accesses. Initial facts are reported under configuration.pnp_devices[].resources with lossless physical-address strings; runtime bank values are observed through actual guest I/O instead of a duplicate public state model.

The original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_resources.c uses optional NEVERD_WDM_RESOURCE_FIXTURE/NEVERD_WDM_RESOURCE_CFG_FIXTURE and true scalar/REP accessors. Native normal/active-CFG rebasing covers packed lists, lower completion timing, aliases, page-tail mappings, STOP/restart persistence, independent PDOs, surprise cleanup and invalid accesses. Public C API/CLI reject invalid register facts before image loading and execute the 14-request driver-register-bank-scenario.json through two START epochs, preserving returned IOCTL bytes and exact map/unmap counts. C V1 struct and Python ctypes are unchanged because scenario_json is shared. Missing genuine artifacts skip explicitly; evidence remains Linux-only.

DriverResources.h / DriverResources.def and DriverInterrupts.h / DriverInterrupts.def define fixed register_bank memory and interrupt assignments. DriverScenario owns JSON/native preflight; DriverResult records initial configuration without duplicating observed bank state. KernelResources alone owns packed raw/translated assignments, resource epochs, physical presence and power. KernelMMIO owns persistent register values and independent mapping aliases; KernelInterrupts owns opaque connections, locks, captured pulses and explicit level-source state. KernelModelResources builds read-only START packets and integrates actual provider completion: successful lower START publishes its epoch before upper callbacks, and actual provider device-SET updates D0/D2/D3 accessibility. Failed START or STOP/REMOVE teardown is checked before terminal IRP completion, after upper callbacks can unmap and disconnect, without implicit cleanup. Surprise removal immediately denies hardware access. GuestMemory and UnicornBackend validate whole CPU/API transactions before MMIO effects and preserve the first fault latch. Fixed-assignment restart preserves bank values. Arbitrary RAM, resource rebalance, ports, message/passive interrupts and other DMA interfaces remain unsupported.

KernelInterrupts binds each pulse or level transition to captured connection tokens and resource epochs at successful request submission; per-source assertions combine into a shared line with explicit positive sampling intervals. KernelModelInterruptEvents preflights all same-time producer capacities before clock advancement or observation mutation, including exact framework cancellation callback counts; timers, provider completion and cancellation cannot silently consume the space reserved for an ISR. Actual provider hardware publication precedes pulse eligibility, and admitted interrupts precede DPCs and passive callbacks. The schedule remains cooperative: virtual time advances only while idle, and zero delay does not mean instruction preemption. KernelModelInterrupts decodes the legacy eleven-argument ABI and selected Ex fields, while KernelGuestCall gives interrupt callbacks a separate owner/token. ISR and synchronization callbacks hold the same nonrecursive lock at synchronization IRQL, while scheduling uses the assigned hardware DIRQL; nested CPU frames preserve caller IRQL/CR8, and BOOLEAN uses only AL. Manual locks require the same execution identity and saved IRQL, and a callback cannot return with a leaked lock. Armed pulses outlive their source IRP; disconnected, unavailable-epoch or non-D0 delivery records an explicit undelivered reason and stops, with no rebind or invented enable/ack register behavior. DriverResult.Interrupts contains independent observations, never synthetic IRPs or NTSTATUS completions.

The same register_bank provider can declare interrupts alone or alongside resources; at least one list must be nonempty. resource_free rejects an explicit interrupts field, including []. Each interrupt requires id, raw_vector, raw_level, raw_affinity, translated_vector, translated_level, translated_affinity, mode (latched or level_sensitive) and share (device_exclusive or shared). A level source also requires positive retrigger_after_100ns; latched sources reject that field. DriverInterrupts.h / DriverInterrupts.def own the spellings and limits: 8 interrupts per PDO / 32 total, per-PDO unique bounded ASCII IDs, raw level 0–65535 and translated DIRQL 3–12. Both affinity masks must be 1, making CPU0/group0 explicit. Vectors retain all 32 bits without a guessed IRQL relation. A translated vector can be shared only with matching level, affinity, mode and sampling period. Memory descriptors precede ordered interrupt descriptors, whose sharing and level/latched flags reflect the assignment. This models declared synthetic lines, not a PCI controller.

READ/WRITE/IOCTL requests may declare interrupt_events, each with explicit after_100ns, device_id and interrupt_id. Optional action defaults to pulse for existing latched scenarios. Level sources require assert or deassert; latched sources require pulse. Other request kinds reject the field even when empty. At most 64 events per request / 1024 total are accepted, with nonnegative delay through INT64_MAX. Successful submission captures the live connections and PDO resource epoch. Source IRP completion does not cancel an event. Due events run at supported callback boundaries; time advances only while idle, without instruction-level preemption. Provider hardware publication precedes eligibility, and ISRs precede DPCs/workers according to assigned DIRQL. A lost connection, stale/unavailable epoch or physical D3 records an undelivered_reason and stops without rebinding the event. A shared latched pulse invokes every captured ISR in registration order, even when an earlier handler claims it. Level lines retain one asserted state per PDO/source/epoch; the shared physical line is the OR of those sources. All same-time source changes apply before sampling. A still-asserted line is sampled again after its declared interval, so a repeated assertion does not invent an edge. Claiming a level interrupt stops that sample's handler search but does not acknowledge the device or clear any source. Only explicit deassert changes that source's state. A session permits at most 4096 delivery batches, in addition to shared callback and instruction budgets; exhaustion fails before another delivery. Disconnect and device retirement reject a still-asserted source. Register writes never infer an enable or acknowledgement protocol.

IoConnectInterrupt uses its eleven arguments and the exact translated assignment. IoConnectInterruptEx supports FullySpecified (1), LineBased (2, one assigned line on the explicit PDO) and FullySpecifiedGroup (4, group 0); disconnection requires the matching version/context. Registration and disconnection require PASSIVE_LEVEL. A private lock or an initialized caller-provided nonpaged lock is supported. Multiple connections can share the caller's lock with the same synchronization IRQL, which must be at least each assigned DIRQL; it does not change scheduler priority. LineBased zero selects the assigned level. CPU0/group0 and no floating-state save remain required. KINTERRUPT is opaque. The real ISR receives (Interrupt, ServiceContext) and returns BOOLEAN from AL; FALSE is a valid unclaimed observation. KeSynchronizeExecution runs the actual callback under the same lock at synchronization IRQL, restoring caller IRQL/CR8 afterward. Manual acquire/release enforce nonrecursive ownership, original execution and saved IRQL. Connected locks cannot be accessed through executive spin-lock APIs or outlive their storage. DIRQL waits, floating-state save and instruction-level preemption remain unsupported. Failed START and successful STOP/REMOVE require disconnection before terminal completion; disconnect never silently discards queued DPCs.

Reports retain declared resources in configuration.pnp_devices[].interrupts and flatten events in configuration.interrupt_events. Observed interrupts rows retain source_request_index, event_index, device_id, interrupt_id, action, epoch, due_at_100ns, nullable occurred_at_100ns, delivered_at_100ns, returned_at_100ns, interrupt_object, return_value, claimed and undelivered_reason. handlers records each actual callback, including its delivery_index for repeated samples. A deassertion records its occurrence without fabricating an ISR return. The row's claimed result aggregates actual handlers; an unclaimed interrupt remains valid. The runnable [interrupt scenario](examples/driver-interrupt-scenario.json) uses genuine-WDK driver_wdm_interrupts.c through optional NEVERD_WDM_INTERRUPT_FIXTURE / NEVERD_WDM_INTERRUPT_CFG_FIXTURE. Normal/CFG and preferred/rebased tests cover shared pulses, caller-provided locks and level assertion/repetition/deassertion. The existing C/Python scenario_json boundary and neverd_driver_options_v1 layout are unchanged. Missing artifacts skip explicitly; execution evidence remains Linux-only.

DriverDMA.h / DriverDMA.def add an optional dma object to a register_bank PDO, alongside its memory/interrupt assignments; DMA alone does not replace either resource list. All seven fields are explicit: address_bits (32 or 64), maximum_length (1–1048576 bytes), map_registers (1–256), alignment (power of two from 1–4096), logical_base (nonzero and page aligned), logical_length (page aligned, 4096–1073741824 bytes), and Boolean scatter_gather. The overflow-free aperture must fit the address width. Each PDO has an independent logical domain, so equal addresses on different devices do not alias. Translated MMIO resources must avoid the reserved model RAM range [0x1000000000, 0x1004000000). These declarations describe a coherent synthetic bus master, never host physical memory or a PCI device.

IoGetDmaAdapter accepts the historical DEVICE_DESCRIPTION version 0/1 fields for an Internal bus master and publishes a version-one DMA_ADAPTER with its actual 104-byte DMA_OPERATIONS table. Version 2/3 probes return NULL without reading a modern description tail. Each indirect method is bound to that exact live adapter, independently of kernel imports. Implemented methods are AllocateCommonBuffer, FreeCommonBuffer, GetDmaAlignment, GetScatterGatherList, PutScatterGatherList, PutDmaAdapter, AllocateAdapterChannel, MapTransfer, FlushAdapterBuffers and FreeMapRegisters. FreeAdapterChannel and ReadDmaCounter remain named traps because this profile has no subordinate/system DMA controller. Common-buffer allocation/free and alignment queries require PASSIVE_LEVEL; Get/PutScatterGatherList require DISPATCH_LEVEL, and adapter release permits IRQL through DISPATCH_LEVEL. x64 ignores CacheEnabled. Unsupported version probes, incompatible declared capabilities and documented allocation shortages return NULL; malformed or unmodeled interface selections and backend failures remain explicit errors.

KernelPhysicalMemory assigns at most 16384 model physical pages of 4096 bytes to existing RAM. CPU virtual addresses, physical page identities and device logical addresses are distinct. Built MDL PFN arrays expose these shared identities read-only; unbuilt descriptors have no usable PFNs. Small neighboring allocations may share a PFN but retain separate byte ranges and lifetimes. Common buffers, pool storage and request buffers use the same bytes already owned by GuestMemory, without a second DMA copy. A live SG mapping pins its exact data range and descriptor. Completion, pool/MDL free and teardown reject live dependencies before retirement. Unmapping a direct MDL only revokes its CPU system mapping; DMA remains able to reach its locked backing. DmaWritable records the write-lock contract separately from CPU mapping permissions: device writes require direct READ/OUT_DIRECT or writable nonpaged storage; WRITE/IN_DIRECT do not gain that permission merely because their CPU mapping is writable.

GetScatterGatherList validates CurrentVa/Length against the MDL's original range and creates logical page fragments over its existing backing. Available map registers allow the real four-argument void AdapterListControl to run inline before the API returns; otherwise admission retains the data/descriptor and reserves a callback in the PDO's FIFO until resources are released. This profile has no StartIo ownership, so the callback's second IRP argument is NULL. Callback return does not release a mapping. CPU access to a live SG data range requires Put first; a callback waiting for map registers has not yet granted the device ownership of those bytes. PutScatterGatherList may run inside the callback; after Put, the driver may complete the request and release the last adapter while its callback continuation and device hold survive until return. Common buffers require their original adapter, length, logical address and CPU address when freed. Logical addresses are never reused during the session, including restart. A resource wait without a real producer stalls explicitly; it does not fabricate a completion or deadline.

Only READ/WRITE/IOCTL requests accept dma_events. Each event requires after_100ns, device_id, logical_address, direction and length; write_memory additionally requires exact-length data_hex, while read_memory rejects that field. Directions are from the device's perspective. Limits are 64 events per request, 1024 total, 16 MiB of total transaction bytes and 1 MiB per transaction; delay is nonnegative through INT64_MAX. Submission captures the PDO's current assigned epoch and anchors virtual time, but does not require a mapping that the forthcoming dispatch has yet to create. Delivery resolves the complete live logical range and direction, requires physical D0, and validates all backing bytes before any transaction effect. Source IRP completion does not cancel an event. Missing/released mappings, stale epochs, surprise removal or non-D0 power record a failure and stop; events neither rebind nor invent an interrupt, register protocol or IRP completion. At one scheduled boundary, provider hardware publication precedes DMA bytes, which precede independently declared interrupt pulses. Timing remains cooperative, not instruction-level preemption.

Reports retain configuration.pnp_devices[].dma and flattened configuration.dma_events. Root dma_transfers rows identify source_request_index, event_index, device_id, epoch, logical_address, direction, length and due_at_100ns, with nullable occurred_at_100ns, completed_at_100ns, mapping, adapter and failure_reason; data_hex contains actual transferred bytes. Every declared transaction must finish without failure for scenario_success. The DMA scenario uses original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_dma.c with optional NEVERD_WDM_DMA_FIXTURE / NEVERD_WDM_DMA_CFG_FIXTURE, exercising a common buffer through actual adapter pointers and a separately declared ISR→DPC completion. C/Python still use scenario_json without changing neverd_driver_options_v1. Missing artifacts skip explicitly; evidence is Linux-only. Subordinate controllers, V2/V3 methods, hardware descriptor engines, general KMDF DMA and other device models remain unsupported.

DriverDMA.h / DriverDMA.def own explicit per-PDO capabilities and independent external transactions. KernelPhysicalMemory registers exact live RAM allocations, assigns shared page identities and pins byte ranges; MDLs are views of that authority, not copied buffers. GuestMemory / UnicornBackend provide whole-span backing access that bypasses CPU permissions without changing them, rejects MMIO/running/reentrant or faulted access, and latches unexpected backend failures. KernelDMA owns independent logical domains, adapter-bound method identities, common/SG mappings, map-register admission and callback references; KernelDMAEvents resolves captured PDO epochs at actual delivery. KernelModelPhysicalMemory, KernelModelDMA and KernelModelDMATransfers bridge original allocation/MDL ownership and real indirect guest callbacks. Available SG resources permit inline delivery, while queued callbacks reserve identity and capacity until FIFO promotion. Mapping and callback lifetimes are separate: Put can release data/descriptor pins before callback return, and callback retention does not keep completed IRPs alive. DmaWritable records lock intent independently of CPU mapping permissions. Same-time provider publication precedes DMA RAM effects and then interrupt eligibility. Resource epochs/presence/power remain solely in KernelResources; DMA does not infer vendor registers, assert an IRQ, complete an IRP or own a second lifecycle. Logical addresses are never recycled, and transaction validation failures retain observations without changing RAM. The first interface is coherent common-buffer and version-one SG DMA over bounded model RAM; general hardware, subordinate controllers and other DMA interfaces remain unsupported.

AllocateAdapterChannel requires DISPATCH_LEVEL and reserves an opaque non-NULL map-register token. Common buffers, SG lists and channel reservations share the same per-PDO quota and FIFO. Success accepts a real immediate or queued AdapterControl; an excessive requested count returns STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES without a callback. One unfinished allocation callback is allowed per guest device, and calling AllocateAdapterChannel from AdapterControl is rejected, including through a nested callback. The callback's four arguments contain the actual DEVICE_OBJECT.CurrentIrp snapshot taken at registration. That exact eight-byte field is writable on guest devices; zero or a live IRP routed to the device is accepted. A queued callback retains that packet until entry, after which the callback may complete it. The profile still has no StartIo; the separate SG callback's unused IRP argument remains NULL.

AdapterControl returns a 32-bit IO_ALLOCATION_ACTION; high RAX bits are ignored, and the action never replaces AllocateAdapterChannel's STATUS_SUCCESS. DeallocateObject releases unused or fully flushed registers on callback return. DeallocateObjectKeepRegisters retains them until FreeMapRegisters uses the exact adapter, token and original count. Returning KeepObject requires an unmodeled system controller and fails explicitly. The newly delivered allocation cannot be freed as retained before its callback returns; a different previously retained allocation may be freed when its own contract permits. Callback identity, retained registers and active mapped bytes have separate lifetimes, all checked before adapter or device teardown.

MapTransfer and FlushAdapterBuffers permit IRQL through DISPATCH_LEVEL; channel allocation and register free require DISPATCH_LEVEL. MapTransfer takes an MDL-relative index, reads and updates an actual ULONG length and returns the logical address by value. The bounded SG profile returns one backing-page fragment per call; contiguous subsequent indices in the same MDL and direction extend one operation. Non-SG maps the entire requested extent in one call if it fits the reserved count, without shortening it. The first map reserves a nonreused logical aperture sized to the register reservation; other allocations can interleave without overlapping it. All fragments share one growing physical pin. Device transactions can span the full currently mapped operation, while CPU access, MDL free and completion that retires pinned storage remain blocked until aggregate flush. Flush must match the initial index, MDL, direction and total actual mapped length. It releases mapped bytes without releasing registers, so the retained token can support another operation. Partial flushes, mixed-MDL operations and other MapTransfer patterns are outside this profile, rather than assumed invalid on every Windows system.

KeFlushIoBuffers validates a live locked/nonpaged MDL. The modeled platform is coherent, so either ReadOperation or DmaOperation value needs no separate cache copy; this call does not release DMA ownership or replace FlushAdapterBuffers. The channel scenario runs original driver_wdm_dma_channel.c through two MapTransfer calls, one cross-page device transaction, a separately declared IRQ/DPC, aggregate flush and exact register release. Genuine normal/CFG images use NEVERD_WDM_DMA_CHANNEL_FIXTURE and NEVERD_WDM_DMA_CHANNEL_CFG_FIXTURE.

The original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_dma_channel.c and optional NEVERD_WDM_DMA_CHANNEL_FIXTURE/NEVERD_WDM_DMA_CHANNEL_CFG_FIXTURE exercise real translated bus-master channel calls, aggregate fragments, retained-register reuse and shared common/SG/channel admission. Native normal/CFG/rebased runs and the seven-request C API/CLI example validate the bounded profile; Python uses the same scenario_json interface. Missing fixtures skip explicitly and evidence remains Linux-only.

ExRaiseStatus, ExRaiseAccessViolation and ExRaiseDatatypeMisalignment produce typed guest exceptions without a normal API return. ExRaiseStatus uses only the low NTSTATUS dword; the wrappers use STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION and STATUS_DATATYPE_MISALIGNMENT. The selected profile follows the individual Microsoft DDI ceilings APC_LEVEL for ExRaiseStatus and PASSIVE_LEVEL for the wrappers, while acknowledging that some WDK SAL annotations permit APC_LEVEL for the wrappers. API traces retain a null result and record the raised code in detail.

KernelSEH plans bounded x64 version-one C search/unwind over existing loader metadata, executes real guest filters and exited finally callbacks, and restores supported nonvolatile GPR saves across helpers. Filters receive stable exception/context records on a private stack; original full CPU state survives callbacks. Zero searches, positive selects a handler, and negative can resume an admitted user read/write CPU fault with validated INTEGER/CONTROL changes. Parent thread/process identity and existing user-access authority are preserved, without granting authority to unrelated workers. Actual handlers and enclosing-handler reraises execute. Nested filters and collided finally unwinding preserve explicit logical stack segments and linked exception records. Validated chains, partial prologues, canonical epilogues and complete XMM6-XMM15 restores are supported. API-raise continuation, GS/C++ personalities and incomplete records fail explicitly. Uncaught API/user exceptions are model_error; unrelated backend faults remain terminal. METHOD_NEITHER uses explicit requestor-owned user buffers, checked probes, independent MDL locks and shared kernel aliases; KMDF caller-context accessors and locked WDFMEMORY retain the same ownership rules.

The original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_seh.c with /GS- C routines and explicit GS assembly uses optional NEVERD_WDM_SEH_FIXTURE and NEVERD_WDM_SEH_CFG_FIXTURE. Native normal/active-CFG/rebased cases exercise all three exports, helper nonvolatile restoration, nested and reraised handlers, real filter/search/unwind ordering, guest exception records, supported CPU-fault continuation, full CPU restoration and foreground/worker/attached-worker identity and authority. __GSHandlerCheck_SEH validates fixed and dynamically aligned stack cookies during search and again during unwind, with flags separate from wrapped C handlers. Original GS frames also execute the linked WDK checker; native, C API and Python distinguish valid cookies from corruption before handler execution. Standalone __GSHandlerCheck validates cookie-only frames during search and unwind without adding C scopes. Exact symbol or import identity is required; anonymous instruction patterns and cookie-shaped payloads do not establish this personality. GS/C++ wrappers and C++ exception personalities remain unsupported. Nested filters and collided finally callbacks execute; unrelated CPU faults fail explicitly. C API/CLI runs docs/examples/driver-seh-scenario.json with null raised-call results and actual handler messages. pluginsdk/python/tests/test_driver_seh_integration.py uses the existing JSON binding and optional NEVERD_TEST_LIBNEVERD / NEVERD_TEST_WDM_SEH_FIXTURE / NEVERD_TEST_WDM_SEH_CFG_FIXTURE inputs. Missing fixtures skip explicitly; evidence is Linux-only and does not establish general SEH.

The original genuine-WDK driver_wdm_neither.c uses optional NEVERD_WDM_NEITHER_FIXTURE and NEVERD_WDM_NEITHER_CFG_FIXTURE. Native normal/active-CFG and preferred/rebased runs verify six packet/probe/CPU-fault/locked-MDL paths. Backend and request-owner tests verify shared alias bytes, independent pins, write protection, completion output and terminal kernel faults. C API/CLI and Python execute docs/examples/driver-neither-scenario.json and verify plain and locked-alias output bytes. Missing external images skip explicitly; Linux evidence does not establish arbitrary Windows process memory.

A nonempty WDM METHOD_NEITHER IOCTL may independently set user_input_access and user_output_access to read_write (default), read_only or no_access. These explicit page facts are applied after buffer initialization and before guest dispatch. No-access still retains a non-NULL caller pointer and RAM backing, so ProbeForRead can pass its numerical check before a CPU read faults, while ProbeForWrite and MmProbeAndLockPages raise access violations according to page rights. Strict JSON/native validation rejects rights on buffered/direct IOCTLs, wrong directions, empty buffers, unknown values and wrong types. The original WDK fixture runs CPU/probe/MDL negative paths through normal/CFG and preferred/rebased images; C/CLI/Python observe completed failing statuses without terminal backend faults. Caller-context restrictions keep raw user pointers unavailable in ordinary workers; a work item with a live requesting IRP can explicitly attach to that process for bounded raw user-memory access, while locked MDL system aliases remain independently usable. Optional user_unmap_after_dispatch revokes original and declared user virtual access after dispatch returns and before queued work/cancellation; locked MDL aliases retain physical bytes and an unmapped output has no caller-visible output_hex. Synthetic requestor_process_id distinguishes bounded caller contexts; IoGetRequestorProcessId retains the file IRP identity and PsGetCurrentProcessId distinguishes foreground from modeled system work-item execution. requestor_exit_after_dispatch revokes every original and declared VA of that identity before callbacks, while pinned MDL aliases can still complete or cancel. Later new I/O from an exited identity is rejected; explicit CLEANUP/CLOSE remain available, with no inferred handle rundown or cancellation. Arbitrary process address spaces, attachment outside system work items, unmap timing and reuse of original scenario allocation addresses remain unsupported.

READ/WRITE on a WDM device with neither DO_BUFFERED_IO nor DO_DIRECT_IO uses the original caller address only through IRP.UserBuffer. WRITE carries initialized user input and READ a separate user output; neither creates a SystemBuffer or implicit MDL. User page rights apply to WRITE input or READ output only, and explicit rights on a buffered/direct device stop before guest dispatch. A genuine WDK normal/CFG fixture probes and accesses both directions under x64 SEH, including read-only/no-access failures, at preferred and rebased image addresses. C API, CLI and Python observe the same report bytes and request statuses. Deferred raw access still requires locking; general process address spaces remain unsupported.

The genuine WDK neither fixture marks an IOCTL pending after user MDLs are locked in caller context. Its PASSIVE_LEVEL work item reads/writes only through the shared kernel aliases, unlocks and frees the MDLs and work item, then completes the original IRP. The separate raw-user-pointer worker path stops explicitly because queued work does not inherit the requesting process context; an explicit IoGetRequestorProcess / KeStackAttachProcess / KeUnstackDetachProcess pair can access a live requestor with matching APC storage. Native normal/CFG preferred/rebased, C API/CLI and Python paths distinguish these outcomes; exited requestors, unmatched APC states and complex operations while attached fail explicitly. Scheduled WDM cancellation and driver-initiated IoCancelIrp use one IRP.Cancel/CancelRoutine state; a registered callback runs with the cancel spin lock held at DISPATCH_LEVEL, must release with CancelIrql before completion or return, and is ordered before pending workers. Genuine WDK normal/CFG/rebased, C API/CLI and Python cases cover canceled locked MDLs, completion-first, synchronous return values and an invalid IRQL release.

METHOD_NEITHER IOCTL and neither READ/WRITE accept explicit request-local user_buffers and user_pointers. Declarations contain bounded ID, nonzero size, zero-padded initial bytes and read_write/read_only/no_access rights. References select input/output/memory plus offset, with an ID only for memory. Eight-byte x64 source slots may be unaligned but cannot overlap or exceed their buffer; targets may be interior or one-past. Aliased and cyclic pointer graphs share actual RAM without inferring private driver layouts. Shared strict JSON/native preflight enforces 64 additional buffers, 256 pointer slots, 64-byte IDs, 64 KiB per buffer and the existing 512 KiB total buffer budget. Runtime rejects declarations on buffered/direct READ/WRITE before dispatch.

Declared user regions use the existing process-owned allocation and physical backing authority. Completion does not revoke the original VA; explicit request unmap revokes all of that request’s original and declared regions, while process exit includes completed allocations from the same PID. Independent MDL or WDFMEMORY aliases retain pinned bytes until unlock/completion. WDF probing accepts the current request’s declared regions only in caller context. configuration.user_memory preserves declarations and source_request_index; requests[].user_buffers reports ID, address, size, access, revoked and backing_hex. The backing snapshot is diagnostic RAM at stop, including after terminal faults, and does not imply caller-visible output or restored access. GuestMemory.snapshotBacking validates the whole span, reads adapter-owned RAM without engine reentry, rejects running/device-callback/MMIO access and preserves the first fault. Arbitrary mappings, cross-request IDs and remapping the original declared scenario allocations remain unsupported.

Original WDK WDM/KMDF nested-user fixtures exercise two-level structures, duplicate aliases and interior offsets, caught read-only failures, WDM locked workers after unmap/process exit, and WDF caller-context locking before queue delivery. Native cases run normal/CFG and preferred/rebased images; C API/CLI/Python share docs/examples/driver-nested-user-scenario.json and assert diagnostic bytes after revocation. Missing external fixtures skip explicitly; execution evidence remains Linux-only.

IoBuildPartialMdl supports subranges, zero-length remainder, PFN capacity checks, source-independent nonpaged descriptors and separate root-lock/system-alias ownership. Target reuse uses the genuine MmPrepareMdlForReuse inline path. Completion preflights all dependencies before releasing chains in either order; live DMA prevents rebuild or retirement. MmMapLockedPagesSpecifyCache(UserMode) creates independent process-owned NX/read-only-capable views of existing private physical pages at IRQL <= APC_LEVEL without changing MappedSystemVa. Exact pair/process unmapping, canonical alias re-locking, typed resource shortage, process exit and lifetime guards are modeled. Requested addresses preserve page offsets in a bounded reusable arena. Exact unmapping releases address/budget; surviving pins/system aliases retain old backing after VA reuse. Different live processes can own the same VA with independent backing/rights; whole-set process switching preflights alias replacement before publishing context, and another process exit/unmap cannot retire the active view. Live opaque dispatcher objects in outgoing views reject switching. MmNonCached/MmCached/MmWriteCombined requests retain each physical page's existing cache attribute; ordinary model RAM is cached, and conflicting registrations or reserved types fail. Arbitrary virtual-memory allocation, page tables and a general process manager remain unsupported.

The backend-selecting C API and CLI support driver-strict over Unicorn, matching Linux x64 KVM and matching Windows x64 WHP. auto selects matching native execution; explicit Unicorn and the original V1 API preserve the portable software profile. checked-x64-v1 remains an explicit bounded instruction and memory-observation contract. Hardware unavailability and unsupported instructions fail explicitly without fallback. CPU transport availability does not implement the Windows ARM64 driver ABI.

Original built-in and configured WDK images/scenarios are compared against legacy Unicorn under checked Unicorn, KVM and WHP, at original and relocated addresses. The comparison includes negative outcomes, request bytes, API results, writes and final model state; backend metadata, diagnostics and REP instruction-count conventions are excluded.
